name: Bleeding
immediateSteps: Apply firm pressure with a clean cloth or gauze.
Keep your pet calm and restrict movement.
Do not remove impaled objects — stabilise and go immediately.

name: Can't Breathe
immediateSteps: Check mouth for visible obstruction if safe to do so.
Keep airway open; avoid stressing your pet.
Call ahead — oxygen/ICU may be needed.

name: Seizure
immediateSteps: Clear nearby objects; do not restrain the tongue.
Time the episode; note eye movement and salivation.
After it stops, keep warm and transport to emergency vet.

name: Poisoning
immediateSteps: Do not induce vomiting unless a vet instructs you.
Bring packaging or a photo of the substance.
Call the clinic en route — some toxins need specific antidotes.

name: Vomiting
description: Repeated vomiting, won't keep water down
immediateSteps: Withhold food; offer ice chips if directed by phone.
Watch for blood, lethargy, or bloat (distended abdomen).
Seek emergency care if non-stop or with other symptoms.

name: Injury
description: Hit by vehicle, fall, visible fracture
immediateSteps: Muzzle only if needed for safety; support fractures with a splint/towel.
Minimise movement on a flat board or blanket.
Bleeding and shock risk — go to a surgical-capable clinic.

name: Unresponsive
description: Won't wake up, limp, no reaction
immediateSteps: Check breathing and pulse if trained; begin transport.
Keep neck aligned if trauma suspected.
This is always emergency — call while en route.

name: Not Sure
description: Something is wrong but hard to describe
immediateSteps: Note appetite, energy, breathing, and last normal behaviour.
Take a short video if safe — helps triage over the phone.
When in doubt after hours, use a 24/7 clinic.
